# REVISED PROPOSED DECISION OF ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGE: Wildfire Mitigation and Vegetation Management Requirements for Electrical Corporations

This revised proposed decision reflects comments received on the proposed decision and is issued for further public comment. Comments are due 20 days after issuance.

## 1. Purpose and Scope

### 1.1 Purpose
This decision establishes minimum wildfire mitigation and vegetation management requirements for electrical corporations operating overhead facilities in High Fire-Threat Districts.

### 1.2 Applicability
These requirements apply to each electrical corporation serving more than 100,000 customers within the State.

## 2. Definitions

### 2.1 Electrical Corporation
"Electrical corporation" has the meaning set forth in the State Public Utilities Code.

### 2.2 High Fire-Threat District
"High Fire-Threat District" or "HFTD" means an area designated as Tier 2 or Tier 3 on the Commission's fire-threat map.

### 2.3 Public Safety Power Shutoff
"Public Safety Power Shutoff" or "PSPS" means the proactive de-energization of covered facilities to reduce wildfire ignition risk.

### 2.4 Covered Facility
"Covered facility" means any overhead conductor operating at or above 1 kV located within an HFTD.

## 3. Wildfire Mitigation Plans

### 3.1 Plan Required
Each electrical corporation shall file a Wildfire Mitigation Plan (WMP) with the Commission covering a three-year period.

### 3.2 Plan Contents
Each WMP shall describe inspection programs, vegetation management practices, system hardening projects, and situational awareness measures for all covered facilities.

### 3.3 Filing Deadline
The initial WMP shall be filed within 60 days of the effective date of this decision.

## 4. Vegetation Management

### 4.1 Clearance Requirements
Electrical corporations shall maintain a minimum radial clearance of 4 feet between vegetation and covered facilities at all times.

### 4.2 Inspection Reporting
Electrical corporations shall file vegetation inspection reports with the Commission quarterly.

### 4.3 Hazard Tree Removal
Electrical corporations shall remove or mitigate hazard trees identified during inspections within 180 days.

## 5. Public Safety Power Shutoffs

### 5.1 Customer Notification
Electrical corporations shall notify affected customers as soon as practicable before de-energizing covered facilities.

### 5.2 Post-Event Reporting
Electrical corporations shall file a post-event report within 10 business days after each de-energization event.

### 5.3 Medical Baseline Customers
Electrical corporations shall make at least two contact attempts to each medical baseline customer no less than 48 hours before a PSPS event.

## 6. Compliance and Enforcement

### 6.1 Compliance Officer
Each electrical corporation shall designate a compliance officer responsible for implementation of this decision.

### 6.3 Penalties
Violations of this decision are subject to penalties as provided under the State Public Utilities Code.

## 7. Effective Date

### 7.1 Effective Date
If adopted, this decision would become effective 30 days after Commission approval.
